title: Lahaina, Hawaii Travel Guide

hero.headline: Lahaina, Hawaii Travel Guide
hero.subheadline: Context on Lahaina's harbor history, landmarks, and coastal setting on West Maui.

overview: Lahaina is a historic town on the west coast of Maui that served as the Hawaiian Kingdom capital from 1820 to 1845. It later developed as a whaling port and commercial harbor, and many surviving landmarks document that period. The district sits on a dry leeward shoreline with direct access to marine channels between Maui, Lanai, and Molokai. Trip planning often focuses on historic sites, waterfront infrastructure, and regional ferry or excursion access.

thingsToDo.title: Lahaina Historic District
thingsToDo.description: The Lahaina Historic District preserves a concentration of buildings and streets linked to Lahaina's periods as a royal center and nineteenth-century whaling port. Its designation documents the town's role in Hawaiian Kingdom governance, missionary activity, and Pacific maritime trade networks. Visitors experience the district by walking Front Street and nearby civic blocks where many interpretation sites are clustered near the harbor. The area is notable for preserving one of Hawaii's densest collections of structures tied to early state and commercial history.

thingsToDo.title: Banyan Tree Park
thingsToDo.description: Banyan Tree Park is a civic square in Lahaina centered on a large banyan tree planted in 1873 to commemorate the fiftieth anniversary of the first Protestant mission in Lahaina. Over time the tree expanded into a broad canopy supported by multiple aerial trunks, making it one of the largest banyans in the United States. Visitors use the square as a walking stop beside the old courthouse, harbor, and other historic district landmarks. The site is notable because a single planted tree became a defining urban landmark for West Maui.

thingsToDo.title: Lahaina Harbor
thingsToDo.description: Lahaina Harbor is a small-boat harbor on Maui's leeward coast that historically supported shipping, fishing, and inter-island travel. Its waterfront location helped Lahaina function as a commercial port during whaling and later tourism development in West Maui. Visitors today use the harbor for ferry access, offshore excursions, and waterfront views within walking distance of the historic district. The harbor remains notable as the operational maritime core of Lahaina's historic shoreline.

sections.heading: Overview
paragraphs: Lahaina is on Maui's leeward coast and historically functioned as both a royal seat and a Pacific whaling port. The town developed around a protected shoreline used for shipping and fishing, with civic buildings concentrated near the waterfront. Historic district landmarks document nineteenth-century political and commercial periods. Current travel planning centers on open historic areas, harbor access, and nearby West Maui coastal routes.
